# Catalog admission: two explicit contract choices

31 October 2026 UTC. **New independent primary-source analysis only. No option is selected, no implementation or new runtime is authorized, and goal 3 remains unaccepted.** This document contains current technical analysis and finite choices; it does not contain or reconstruct previous failure witnesses, raw outputs, archives or backup preparation. The existing absolute no-extra-database requirement remains in force unless the coordinator/parent explicitly changes and durably records it.

## 1. What must be decided

Two different user properties must not be conflated:

**A — absolute attachment admission:** a planned read must reject when *any* additional user database is attached, including an unused HIDDEN in-memory database. Proving the intended lookup destination is not a substitute for this absence property.

**B — owned-bound lookup admission:** a successful planned read must use the owned main base tables, exact admitted types and trusted pinned callables. An unreachable HIDDEN attachment need not be rejected merely for existing. Visible extra databases and active foreign catalog/schema/search-path states are rejected, but complete attachment absence is expressly not attested.

Choosing B changes an end-user guarantee: a planned read is no longer an exhaustive connection-state/attachment rejection check. It may succeed with an unused hidden attachment. Neither choice is a hostile Python/C++ sandbox, an unmanaged-concurrent-query guarantee, or full resource accounting. B cannot be selected simply by changing a checker's expectation.

## 3. A protected first inspection is justified under either choice

Use fully specified `system.main` inspectors for the initial primitive existential. A fully specified catalog/schema yields one lookup; the dedicated system catalog is not an arbitrary attached alias. Ordinary CREATE cannot target the system catalog, ordinary replacement cannot acquire an internal-drop permission, and ordinary DROP rejects an internal entry. These are separate authority facts, not merely an inference from the spelling `system`. [Catalog lookup](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/catalog/catalog.cpp#L81-L100), [one qualified lookup](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/catalog/catalog.cpp#L677-L725), [CREATE target rejection](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/planner/binder/statement/bind_create.cpp#L327-L332), [replacement](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/catalog/catalog_entry/duck_schema_entry.cpp#L136-L151), [DROP](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/planner/binder/statement/bind_drop.cpp#L90-L99).

A first query made only of protected functions/tables/views sources, literal 1, `internal IS FALSE`, the temporary Boolean test, AND, UNION ALL and LIMIT 1 avoids an overridable count/count_star/current_setting dependency *before* rejecting user callables. IS Boolean tests use a directly specified `LogicalType::BOOLEAN` cast and a typed comparison. LIMIT binding chooses `LogicalType::BIGINT` directly, not a SQL typename lookup. This remains a trusted-engine/cast-registry premise, not a defense against native callback replacement. [Boolean lowering](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/parser/peg/transformer/transform_expression.cpp#L699-L704), [comparison](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/parser/peg/transformer/transform_expression.cpp#L824-L832), [LIMIT type](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/planner/binder/query_node/bind_select_node.cpp#L56-L78).

That first query must precede database/session/schema/clock inspections, after the existing BEGIN and post-getter readiness check. Fully drain and validate its owned result shape. Any match rejects; errors or unexpected shape roll back and propagate, with no automatic native fallback. LIMIT bounds this guard's answer, not a user's query result. It does not prove that every metadata source stops enumeration early.

## 4. Conditional lookup closure: what the pin actually establishes

### 4.1 Active context and ordinary main-schema lookup

`SetPathsInternal` installs temp.main, explicit set paths, the default catalog's main, system.main and system.pg_catalog, plus trusted extension schemas in system. `GetCatalogsForSchema(main)` selects main-schema entries, while unqualified lookups consider the whole relevant path. Thus the shorthand “temp/owned/system main” is correct for main-qualified lookup, but omits pg_catalog/extension schemas for unqualified callable lookup. [Path construction](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/catalog/catalog_search_path.cpp#L274-L304), [defaults](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/catalog/catalog_search_path.cpp#L333-L354).

Protected current_database reads the connection's actual default-database resolution; protected current_schema reads its default path entry. Protected search_path reads the serialized explicit set paths, including a nonempty catalog qualifier rather than silently dropping it. These are fresh statements, not an authorization cache. Accepting only the existing empty/main explicit path, main schema, the sole visible owned path and matching current database is therefore a conservative active-context condition. A USE/foreign path cannot be admitted merely because hidden metadata omits that catalog. Settings remain mutable client/global state, not MVCC data. [Context functions](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/extension/core_functions/scalar/generic/system_functions.cpp#L23-L33), [default database](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/main/database_manager.cpp#L487-L526), [path serialization](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/main/settings/custom_settings.cpp#L1556-L1579), [entry rendering](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/catalog/catalog_search_path.cpp#L22-L48).

Two-part main.table also undergoes schema-versus-attached-catalog resolution. New ordinary aliases main, temp and system are reserved, with case-insensitive identifier equality; this closes the ordinary hidden-main alias concern. It does not prove absence of other hidden aliases. [Two-part binding](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/planner/binder/statement/bind_create.cpp#L70-L109), [reserved aliases](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/main/attached_database.cpp#L225-L227), [new-attach check](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/main/database_manager.cpp#L198-L200), [identifier equality](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/common/identifier.cpp#L26-L39).

### 4.2 Non-table implicit-catalog fallback is not an all-catalog search

The engine has an additional fallback for unqualified non-table names only when normal lookup found nothing. It examines catalogs explicitly flagged as implicit search catalogs, not every hidden attachment. `GetImplicitSearchCatalogs` selects path entries with a catalog and an empty schema; the allowed ordinary empty/main context creates no such foreign entry. Trusted extension schemas added by normal path construction are explicitly system-qualified, not arbitrary attached catalogs. Moreover the fixed builtin/native names required by the admitted executor have positive normal-path resolutions, so the `!result.Found()` condition is false. Main-qualified functions disable this unqualified fallback entirely. [Fallback condition](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/catalog/catalog.cpp#L1217-L1223), [fallback implementation](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/catalog/catalog.cpp#L1303-L1323), [path selection](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/catalog/catalog_search_path.cpp#L298-L304).

This is conditional on the genuine pinned helper/core registration and no arbitrary privileged host alteration. Missing capabilities remain errors/UNRUN, never a guessed alternate callable. All trust-stage metadata/context callable names should nevertheless be protected by system.main qualification. Existing generated main-qualified scalars and inherited fixed builtins may rely on the proven post-guard path/positive-resolution condition; globally rewriting every function is not necessary merely because a hidden aux exists.

### 4.3 Unqualified TABLE fallback refutes broad noninterference

Unqualified table binding is different. Even when normal lookup found an owned table, the engine checks a catalog *named like that table* for a default table and raises ambiguity if both are found. This lookup is outside the ordinary schema path. AttachOptions recognizes a default_table option. Therefore an unused hidden catalog is not universally semantically inert merely because search_path/current_database are unchanged. [Table fallback/ambiguity](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/catalog/catalog.cpp#L1199-L1213), [named-catalog lookup](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/catalog/catalog.cpp#L1277-L1298), [option parsing](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/main/attached_database.cpp#L85-L95).

Classification matters: **when the owned base table is present and actually attested**, the inspected path throws before returning either entry; it does not silently choose the hidden default table. That is fail-closed ambiguity, but it can occur at inherited DESCRIBE/schema-version/td_clock/native FROM temporal_facts dependencies. Search-path checks alone do not promise rejection before every such client-relative helper, nor identical errors/success for all hidden states. If owned-table presence is not established, the default-table fallback can return another table; do not drop the exact base-table admission premise.

Schema qualification main.table disables this fallback: allow_default_lookup is true only when both catalog and schema are absent. Compiler-generated CTE names bind to their local CTE before catalog table lookup. [Qualification condition](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/catalog/catalog.cpp#L1131-L1133), [CTE-first binding](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/planner/binder/tableref/bind_basetableref.cpp#L142-L182).

Thus B has two honest strengths to choose between: (B1) successful-read ownership, permitting propagated ambiguity errors from unchanged legacy helpers; or (B2) stronger planned-path lookup pinning, which must separately address every inherited unqualified table dependency. B2 cannot be claimed while retaining the current unqualified native tail unchanged without an additional integration design. No new native evaluator tail or legacy API change is selected here.

### 4.4 SQL type names: a resolved proof obligation, not a new demonstrated defect

Parsed SQL casts are UNBOUND TypeExpressions, and type binding searches catalog entries before its final system fallback. A callable-only inventory does not enumerate TYPE_ENTRY objects. However that observation alone does **not** establish ordinary builtin-type shadowing. Every main schema has a DefaultTypeGenerator; recognized builtin names are generated as internal defaults before ordinary CREATE can occupy a vacant name. The fixed names used here—BIGINT, UTINYINT, BOOLEAN, DOUBLE, VARCHAR, BLOB, STRUCT and LIST—are in that builtin set, including at the first temp.main path. Ordinary DROP rejects their internal entries. [Parsed casts](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/parser/peg/transformer/transform_common.cpp#L53-L56), [type lookup](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/planner/binder/expression/bind_type_expression.cpp#L28-L67), [generator installed](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/catalog/catalog_entry/duck_schema_entry.cpp#L76-L84), [builtin names/default flags](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/catalog/default/default_types.cpp#L390-L543), [vacancy protection](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/catalog/catalog_set.cpp#L96-L103).

Under current-pin ordinary SQL plus the allowed path/trusted-host premise, the fixed builtin cast names therefore have source protection. No type-shadow runtime witness was run or is claimed. The initial concern must not be promoted into a defect after this additional source round.

An optional **stronger state policy** is to reject all visible noninternal types with an extra protected primitive duckdb_types arm. Its internal field is physically BOOLEAN; the source scans visible TYPE_ENTRY objects; ordinary type entries copy internal=false and receive an identity constructor when necessary, so metadata is not deliberately omitting ordinary aliases for lack of a constructor. Builtin defaults are internal=true and would not cause a normal false positive. This could conservatively reject unusual pre-existing or historically imported user types, but is broader than the minimal proven current-pin callable fix and incurs another metadata initialization. It needs explicit selection/fixtures, not an invented urgent bypass claim. Hidden types remain omitted and are not globally inventoried. [Types metadata](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/function/table/system/duckdb_types.cpp#L61-L87), [entry constructor/flags](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/catalog/catalog_entry/type_catalog_entry.cpp#L15-L30).

## 5. Snapshot and residual assumptions

CatalogTransaction obtains the active database transaction's snapshot view. CatalogSet scans and name lookups select the entry version through that view. MetaTransaction lazily starts/reuses one transaction per referenced database and retains references; duplicate name reuse by another database in the same transaction is rejected. Keep inspection and execution on the same owned connection and explicit transaction, with no cross-call permission cache. [Catalog view](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/catalog/catalog_transaction.cpp#L8-L11), [version selection](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/catalog/catalog_set.cpp#L542-L552), [scan](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/catalog/catalog_set.cpp#L710-L721), [transaction reuse](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/transaction/meta_transaction.cpp#L60-L84), [reference identity](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/transaction/meta_transaction.cpp#L241-L256).

Do not overextend this: DatabaseManager::GetDatabases(context) actually locks and copies the **current map** plus system/temp. Its header comment suggesting a transaction catalog-set scan is not proof of snapshot stability. Session settings/search paths are also mutable state. A new inventory shim would attest a fresh instant; it would not itself prevent later shared-instance attachment mutation. Public store locking/cooperation, no unmanaged queries/mutations during the admitted call, trusted core/native code and continuously supported FP controls remain required. No new cross-process/concurrent-writer or hostile-host guarantee follows. [Actual inventory loop](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/main/database_manager.cpp#L542-L562).

## 6. A: preserving absolute rejection requires a real new authority

The inspected SQL metadata deliberately filters hidden catalogs. Qualifying its name does not change that behavior. The public v2 catalog module exposes named base-table description, not an all-attachment iterator. A callback context is borrowed and exposes factory/config/filesystem/log, not a public extraction of an arbitrary connection/ClientContext or a hidden-aware attachment list. V1 catalog APIs similarly require a known catalog/entry name; enumerating guessed names cannot prove absence of unknown aliases, and a v1 API is not interchangeable with a v2 handle. [Public v2 context](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb_v2.h#L343-L352), [v2 named description](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/main/capi/v2/capi_v2_catalog.cpp#L13-L40), [v1 known-name lookup](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/main/capi/v1/catalog-c.cpp#L80-L98).

There is a concrete internal C++ authority: DatabaseManager::GetDatabases(context) iterates all attached map entries without IsHidden filtering. Its optional max count can bound discovery of an extra witness rather than transfer an unbounded catalog list. But exposing it requires a separately authorized exact-host C++/host API integration, fresh lifetime/transaction/provenance proof and new reproducible artifact/ABI tests. It is **not already callable through the current pure CAPIv2 helper**. Reinterpreting opaque handle layouts, using another connection, guessing a nonexistent CAPI method, or replacing the current native helper is not an acceptable shortcut.

Possible A work is therefore (a) an independently researched pinned internal C++ inspector with a legitimate same-context entry point and verified actual host linkage; or (b) a host/upstream API that exposes hidden-aware enumeration or enforces the attachment restriction. Neither is implemented, build-gated or proven available here. Public-only construction never issuing ATTACH establishes a narrower cooperating-client invariant; it does not preserve the old absolute rejection guarantee for an ordinarily mutated private connection. If A is mandatory, goal 3 stays blocked until an actual authority and its tests exist.

## 7. B: explicit revised contract draft, not selection

> Planned reads freshly attest a supported owned lookup environment on the same private connection and transaction. Successful evaluation uses the exact owned main base tables and pinned trusted builtin/native callables and types. Visible extra databases and active foreign catalog/schema/search-path states are rejected before client-relative data helpers. Unreachable HIDDEN attachments are not exhaustively inventoried and need not be rejected for their mere existence. Inherited unqualified-table ambiguity may instead fail with rollback; no alternate table, fallback retry or partial output is accepted. No attachment-absence, error/resource noninterference or hostile/concurrent-host guarantee is made.

This draft requires the protected primitive first guard, protected metadata/session functions, exact owned path/schema/base-table presence, positive helper/capability checks and proven fixed generated identifiers/types. A DSL relation/entity/value is never an SQL identifier; IR IDs/parameters remain the only compiler inputs to SQL names/values. It preserves the six-field snapshot, readiness/FP boundaries, all-retained-row validation before visibility/parser, exact tag/string/float semantics, native proof limits, public caps, whole-original-native fallback and no unexpected-error retry.

For **B1**, unchanged inherited table helpers may propagate the source-proved ambiguity error. Do not call all hidden states semantically irrelevant or promise rejection before every clock/helper in this case. For **B2**, root must separately design and freeze main/owned-qualified planned schema inspection, clock and native-table dependencies without silently changing legacy methods or creating a second native evaluator tail. Main qualification has a source proof under the allowed context/reserved aliases; a fully quoted trusted owned-catalog prefix is a stronger alternative, not an excuse to interpolate DSL/user names.

## 8. Finite decision and regression matrix

| Decision or fixture | A | B1 | B2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unused HIDDEN extra with unchanged owned context | Must reject via new authoritative mechanism | May admit; no absence claim | May admit; no absence claim |
| Visible extra / active foreign context or path | Reject | Reject before data helpers | Reject before data helpers |
| Reachable noninternal callable / temp table or view | Protected primitive first reject | Same | Same |
| Hidden default-table alias colliding with an inherited table name | Absolute guard must reject first | Owned-table presence + engine ambiguity fails closed; possibly late | Planned table qualification must remove this binding dependency |
| Fixed builtin SQL types under current-pin ordinary SQL | Preserve default/internal binding | Preserve default/internal binding | Preserve or explicitly protect all such binding |
| Optional visible custom-type policy | Explicitly choose; not implied by callable scan | Same | Same |
| No real hidden-aware API yet | Blocked | Can proceed only after an explicit property revision | Also requires extra planned-table integration design |

Future gated tests must use independently frozen tiny fixtures: clean SQL/native/helper positives; genuine missing-helper negatives; visible callable/temp state rejection; visible versus hidden attachments with unchanged/changed context; default-table alias ambiguity versus qualified resolution; fixed primitive/nested type identities and ordinary creation/drop protection; full-width BIGINT cuts and all typed output bits. Assert actual rejection order where promised, exact successful routes/rows, rollback/health and freshness, not only returned metadata counts. Any setup/SQL availability error is UNAVAILABLE/SETUP_BLOCKED, not proof of either mitigation. No such new test ran in this source-only round.

## 9. Practical cost and stopping condition

The primitive three-source existential can replace the old combined count statement without adding a Python round trip. Metadata still initializes/scans catalog state; functions collection sorts before output. LIMIT 1 bounds the guard row, not all that work. An optional types arm adds another scan/initialization. A correct direct internal A inspector could bound copied attachment witnesses, but its integration cost/ABI risk is much larger and has no measured latency here. B2 may require extra schema plumbing; neither choice warrants a speed claim or an authorization cache. Hidden objects can still change global memory pressure/error behavior, even when they cannot redirect a successful lookup. Existing store/native caps are preserved, not promoted into full connection-resource accounting.

**Next step:** root/parent reviews A versus explicitly revised B, chooses B1/B2 and any optional type-state policy if applicable, and durably records the exact new decision before any app source change. Until then, the old requirement and the implementation hold remain. No additional runtime, source fix, native bridge, backup or remote action is requested by this report.
